title: When the Record Stops Being Email
summary: Securities recordkeeping assumes the record is email. AI assistants create transcripts and summaries nobody retains, and the Los Angeles firm owns that gap.
caption:
Ask a compliance officer where the firm's books and records live and the answer is instant. Ask where the AI notetaker stores its transcripts and the room goes quiet.

The off-channel enforcement wave was never really about texting. It was about firms being unable to supervise or retain something their people already used every day.

Analysis, not prediction: AI assistants rebuild that same gap across a wider surface. A transcript, a summary, a drafted client email — created inside the firm, retained by no one, reviewed by nobody.

The useful response is not a ban. It is an inventory of every surface where client information can be recorded or summarized, a short sanctioned list people will actually use, and identity controls that produce evidence a reviewer can test.

New essay from Pro Link Systems on what supervision looks like when the record stops being email.
